summary: The 2.0 grammar-guide review (ADR-0016 addendum): rulings 2.0:G43 (consonant values), G44 (neighbouring vowels in song) and G45 (foreign names), from the author's answers of 2026-10-18; lumiasa reglossed "Divine Light, Goddess", then "Her Divine Light"; two gloss typos fixed. No grammar rule changes.

rulings.ruling: Vowels are pure, as in Spanish or Italian. l m n s v b d p t f k sound as in English; y as in "yes"; r is a single tap, as in Spanish "pero"; g is always hard, as in "go"; h as in "hope"; z as in "zone". c is always "ch" as in "chant", before every vowel: ca = cha, co = cho, and likewise ce, ci, cu. j is the voiced partner of c, as in "jewel". sh is as in "shade"; ch, written only in a few colour and number words, is the same sound as c.

Every written vowel is its own syllable (0.8:R8), but in singing neighbouring vowels may glide into one note: benaasa may be sung be-na-a-sa or be-naa-sa. The spelling never changes; the songwriter chooses the count the melody needs.
A foreign name is not translated. It is copied as closely as Liraasa letters allow, choosing among near spellings by how the name sounds and sings.
